To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we developed a framework that uses ontology reasoning services and NLG to present relevant ontology structures in order to assist humans with the task of creating semantic annotations for multimedia resources.

we have successfully developed an ontology-based annotation framework for multimedia resources that is able to provide the user with a presentation of relevant ontology structures and to generate natural language descriptions of multimedia resources.

(a) the presentation of ontology structures can be used to support human input in the creation of annotations; (b) the use of ontology reasoning services can be used to identify the relevant ontology structures to be presented to humans; and (c) the presentation of relevant ontology structures can be done in a natural way using natural language generation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an ontology-based system for semi-automatic annotation of multimedia information.
the following question: how to provide support to the user for creating semantic annotations using ontologies.
how to support the process of creating annotations by providing a user with the most relevant information in a way that is both understandable and usable.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

we have developed a framework for semi-automatic semantic annotation of multimedia resources that allows the user to create and maintain ontologies, annotate multimedia information, and use reasoning services and natural-language generation to support this task.
this work has provided the first steps towards a practical solution to the problem of providing human support for the semi-automatic semantic annotation of multimedia resources.
this thesis has provided a basis for further development of a tool to support the annotation process, and that the work is a step towards an automatic annotation process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we are able to provide a user with an overview of the relevant parts of the ontology, and that we are able, in some cases, to generate a natural language description of the ontology that can be used to provide an overview of the ontology.
we have developed an approach for supporting the semi-automatic semantic annotation of multimedia resources.

we have developed a system for supporting human input into the process of creating multimedia annotations, and that we have developed methods for the automatic generation of natural language presentations of relevant information from ontologies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of natural language generation with ontology reasoning can help users to better understand the ontology structures and thus to create better semantic annotations.
the combination of natural language generation and reasoning services provides a powerful means to support human input in the creation of multimedia semantic annotations.

the use of ontology reasoning services can be used to provide a presentation of the information contained in the ontology that is more relevant to the task at hand than the presentation of the entire ontology structure.
